startup.name: Char
startup.one_liner: The AI notepad that knows and works for you
startup.description: Char is a daily notepad that finishes your todos for you. Type a checkbox, and an agent picks it up — researching, drafting, or scheduling on your behalf. Stay in command. Char does the work.

yc_acceptance.basis: Start from about 1 percent with a band of 0.6 to 2 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md). Up: open source with a visible community, a team of three, a distinct idea of tasks completed from checkboxes. Down: productivity and notes is a crowded space with many YC deaths, consumer style usage often lacks repeat paid use (consumer 35 percent inactive), and the founders are based in Seoul and remote. Net about 3 percent.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because AI notepads and meeting assistants are already crowded and the pitch reads as a feature of Notion or Granola. Without strong usage numbers or a paying segment, interviewers would doubt that this notepad beats general assistants on the problems that matter.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only: seed 49% / 59% / 65%, cond 59% (n=126), months_to_seed 3 / 7 / 15 (n=74). Tag AI cohort: 50% / 61% / 67%.
anchors.adjustment_reason: The 59% anchor is for ever reaching seed. The forecast window is 16.3 months (from 2025-07-07 to 2026-11-17), and the cohort median time to seed is 7 months with a 75th percentile of 15 months, so about 60 to 70 percent of eventual seeds land inside it. That gives a window anchor near 0.37 to 0.42, and a round must also exceed $1M, which removes YC-deal-only cases. Set at 0.42, within 1.25 times the window anchor and not lifted for the open source community or the AI label. Meeting and note apps have been crowded and several YC analogs died, which keeps it from rising further. The odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round of $1M to $3M, usually a pre-seed or angel led round that closes quickly. Cohort data for 2022 and later shows a 25th percentile near $2M, and a team this early often takes the first credible check.
Institutional seed of $3M to $6M, the middle of the 2022 and later table (median $3.2M to $3.5M, 75th percentile about $5M) lifted slightly because only rounds above $1M count here.
Hot sector seed of $6M to $12M. The 2026 winners test found 42 percent of confirmed raises here, but that sample leans to press covered rounds, so this band is held below that share.
Upside band above $12M, reached only with fast revenue or a standout founder story. Rare for a team of this size.

ladder.why_it_fails: Window: 16.3 months, to 2026-11-17. Window: 16.3 months, to 2026-11-17. A notepad that completes todos competes with Notion, Granola, Fathom and Circleback, and the strongest YC analogs in this space raised only a seed or sold early while Sidenote, Sonnet and Hypercontext shut down. Investors will want to see weekly active users and a paid conversion rate, and a three person team with an open source product has to prove that people pay. A common outcome is a small angel round under $3M after the batch.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only: series_a cond 26% (n=74), months_to_series_a 22 / 29 / 38 (n=19). Tag AI: cond 23% (n=66).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Same 16.3 month window as the seed step. The 26% anchor is for ever reaching Series A after a seed, but the cohort 25th percentile for reaching Series A is 22 months from batch start, so only about 10 to 15 percent of eventual Series A rounds close inside a window this short. Set at 0.06 given the longer 16 month window and the long timeline to Series A for similar productivity companies.

bands.rationale: Thin or bridge Series A near the 2022 and later 25th percentile of $11M, taken when growth is real but the story is narrow.
Typical Series A, anchored on the 2022 and later median of $14M to $15M and public medians of $17M.
Upside Series A of $20M or more for a category leader with fast ARR growth, as seen in the top AI cases.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A inside 16 months would need rapid paid growth in a category where Granola raised $43M in May 2025 at a $250M valuation and Notion is shipping agents. Fathom reached a Series A years after its batch. Most notepad and meeting companies in the YC data stopped at seed or sold early, so a Series A by November 2026 is unlikely.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2025 --industry B2B --calibration-only: series_b cond 16% (n=19); calibration sample all years: 44% (n=126).
anchors.adjustment_reason: This step is for ever reaching a Series B given a Series A, with no time window, because recent cohorts are right censored. Set between the recent cohort figure of 16% (n=19, few years of follow up) and the all years figure of 44%, at 0.14 for a conservative read.

bands.rationale: Modest Series B near the 25th percentile of the 2022 and later table ($25M to $27M), likely a flat or small step up.
Typical Series B, median $37M to $40M with post money around $600M in the sparse data.
Upside Series B for a breakout. Few cohort examples, so the band is deliberately small.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B requires a standout productivity product with revenue at scale. Notion, Microsoft and Google bundle assistants and meeting tools into products users already pay for, and prosumer productivity apps churn quickly, which caps revenue. Fathom was acquired, and none of the notepad analogs shows a Series B.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only: series_c cond 36% (n=55) across all years. The 2022 to 2025 B2B cohort has no Series C yet (n=3).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Anchor taken from the all years calibration sample because recent cohorts have not had time. Set at 0.25, about 0.7 times the anchor, since most Series B companies in this category face a very crowded late stage market.

bands.rationale: Series C near the 2022 and later 25th percentile ($35M to $50M), in a flat market.
Typical Series C or D, median $74M with post money about $1.2B.
Late stage breakout round. Very few researched cases, so this is a thin tail.

ladder.why_it_fails: Late stage funding would require Char to become a category leader against Notion and Granola, both far ahead on funding. The more likely end for note and agent assistant companies in the data is a small acquisition, an acquihire or a stall at seed stage.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most outcomes are stalls or small sales because notes and todo assistants are bundled into larger suites, users churn between tools, and paid conversion for individuals is low. A path to a larger outcome needs a pivot to a team or enterprise segment with a clear buyer.

analogs.outcome_summary: Winter 2024 company, raised a seed, active.

analogs.outcome_summary: Summer 2023 company, no post YC round, inactive.

killers.risk: Notion, Microsoft, Google and Granola absorb notes plus agent features
killers.evidence: Notion shipped its own transcription in 2025 and Granola raised $43M in May 2025 to add collaboration and agents.
killers.mitigation: Pick a narrow job where completion of the todo is verifiable and own that workflow.

killers.risk: Low willingness to pay for a personal notepad
killers.evidence: Individual productivity apps often have free alternatives and high churn, and YC consumer style apps show high inactivity.
killers.mitigation: Sell to teams with admin features and pricing per seat, track paid retention early.

killers.risk: Agents that act on tasks are unreliable and cause trust failures
killers.evidence: Researching, drafting and scheduling on a user's behalf requires access to email and calendars, and errors lose trust quickly.
killers.mitigation: Keep humans in command with approvals, and start with narrow task types.

competition_now.name: Granola
competition_now.what: AI notepad for meetings with collaboration features and agent features planned.
competition_now.traction: Raised $43M Series B at $250M valuation in May 2025

competition_now.name: Notion
competition_now.what: Workspace that added its own transcription in 2025 and is moving into agents.

competition_now.name: Zoom and Microsoft first party notes
competition_now.what: Built in AI summaries bundled with meeting tools.

technical_complexity.rationale: A notepad with checkbox triggers is easy to build, but reliable agents that research, draft and schedule with calendar and email access need careful permissions and evaluation. A team of three can ship a working version in three months, though quality and trust take longer.

takeover_risk.rationale: Notion and Granola have users, distribution and models, and agent features on top of notes are an obvious next step. A rival needs about six months, and the incentive is strong.

evidence.claim: AI note taking is a funded category: Granola raised $43M in May 2025 and is crowded with first party tools.
The field is crowded, with Zoom and Microsoft bundled tools plus third party apps.

roadmap.goal: Show active daily usage and an example of completed tasks.
actions: Publish the open source repo and track weekly active users
Collect examples of tasks completed without edits
roadmap.proof: 1,000 weekly active users or 30 daily users completing tasks

roadmap.goal: Paid conversion and a clear segment.
actions: Launch paid plans and measure conversion
Choose one segment such as founders or sales teams and ship a template for it
roadmap.proof: $10K monthly recurring revenue and paid retention above 80 percent after three months

roadmap.goal: Prove the agent is the reason users stay, not the notes.
actions: Show task completion rates and time saved
Add team plans with shared workspaces
roadmap.proof: $1M annual recurring revenue growing 15 percent a month

pros.point: Open source with a distinct angle
pros.evidence: The tags list open source, and the concept of a checkbox that triggers an agent is simple and demonstrable.
Granola's 2025 raise shows investors fund AI notepads.

brand.name: Char
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Char" --era 2022+: invented or proper, 4 characters, 1 syllable
weaknesses: Ordinary word with other meanings, hard to search for
brand.rationale: Four letter single syllable names such as Ramp and Brex have worked for startups, and Char is easy to say. A common word is harder to rank in search, so the effect is mildly positive at best.

narrative.headline: A crowded AI notepad with a clear idea, an open source angle and a strong chance of being absorbed by bigger tools.
narrative.general_summary: Char is an open source notepad where typing a checkbox triggers an agent to do the work. The idea is simple and fits where investors are putting money, as Granola's 2025 round showed. The weakness is that Notion, Microsoft and Granola can add the same feature, and several YC note and meeting analogs died or sold small. Over the 16 month window the chance of a round above $1M sits near the cohort window anchor. The odds do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Team of three, open source product, no disclosed traction as of 2025-07-07.
Web results dated after the as of date were ignored.

The seed probability is for a window of 16.3 months and a round above about $1M. It does not rank this company against others: in the 2026 winners test the average seed probability was 0.65 for companies that raised and 0.62 for companies confirmed to have raised nothing beyond the YC deal.
Series B and C plus steps are for ever reaching the round, not inside the window. Reaching a round years later is common for companies with paying customers.
Knowledge base coverage: calibration cohorts are 2022 to 2025 B2B (n=150 researched), with funding coverage partial for most, so known-only rates are biased low.
